name: File metadata (name, size, type, modified time)
plain: Shows name, byte size, MIME type and last modified time of any file the person shares.
meaning: Metadata alone can reveal a lot: camera model names, document names, dates of work. The MIME type comes from the person's OS file associations, which also differs between machines.

web.api: File.name, size, type, lastModified, webkitRelativePath; Blob.slice(), arrayBuffer()

access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
steps: Person shares a file via input, drop, paste or picker
Page can slice and read bytes

limits.headline: Can see the name, size, type and last changed date of files you share
limits.user_action: You pick or drop a file onto the page.
can: See each file's name and size
See its type and last changed date
Check the file before it uploads, and refuse it if too big
cannot: See the full folder path on your computer
See files you did not share
Learn more than that without opening the file's contents

story.what_it_is: Shows the name, size, type and last changed time of any file you share.

marketing.name: File API
marketing.pitch: Documents how a page can read basic details of a file a person has chosen.

story.for_you: The page sees the name, size, kind and last changed time of each file you give it. You never see it read, but it is why an upload checks the size first.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to block files that are too big or of the wrong kind before upload. The same details can reveal when a file was made and what kind of device made it.

use_cases.example: A site refuses a video larger than its limit before you wait for it to upload.
A loan portal checks that your uploads are PDFs or photos, not other file types.
A fraud team reads the last changed time of an uploaded ID photo to see if it was just edited.
A mod site checks the name and size of a mod file for known cheats.
A music tool reads the file name and type to pick a sound format.
A homework site checks that the file was last changed before the deadline.
A document system uses the last changed time to decide which copy is newer.

technical_bounds: Only for files the person selected, dropped or pasted
No full path, owner, creation time or hash; lastModified is milliseconds since epoch (filesystem precision may be 1 s or 2 s)
Firefox resistFingerprinting rounds lastModified (to 100 ms or more) and sets type from extension only
type is guessed from the extension via the OS registry (Chrome, Windows and macOS differ for unknown types such as .md)
EXIF and document properties are not exposed natively but can be parsed by the page from the bytes (GPS in photos)

abuse: Extracting EXIF GPS and device model from photos
